question.text: How many trillion dollar companies will there be on December 18, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of public companies with a market cap over USD $1 trillion on December 18, 2026.
The primary source for this question will be [CompaniesMarketCap](https://companiesmarketcap.com/).
question.fine_print: This question will resolve based upon the number following US market closure at 4:00 PM ET.

research:
I counted **15 companies above $1T on CompaniesMarketCap (CMC) on 2026-11-20**, which is the "15" bucket. Walmart is only about 2.7% above the line, and Samsung is about $100B below it.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-20 (CMC homepage, read directly): the 15 companies over $1T are Apple $5.080T, Microsoft $3.725T, Alphabet $3.422T, NVIDIA $3.414T, Amazon $2.801T, SpaceX $1.805T, TSMC $1.769T, Saudi Aramco $1.707T, Broadcom $1.581T, Meta $1.498T, Tesla $1.473T, Berkshire $1.220T, Eli Lilly $1.211T, Anthropic $1.207T and Walmart $1.027T. [CMC](https://companiesmarketcap.com/)
- The next ones below the line: Samsung $899.75B, JPMorgan $848.25B, AMD $774.00B, Visa $759.05B, Micron $735.90B and SK Hynix $592.26B. [CMC](https://companiesmarketcap.com/)
- How much each name would have to move to cross the line (my arithmetic):
  - Walmart would drop out after a fall of about 2.6%.
  - Anthropic, Lilly and Berkshire each have about 17-18% of room.
  - Samsung needs about +11% to get in, JPM about +18%, AMD about +29% and Micron about +36%.
- CMC's Walmart page shows $1.027T, 15th place, with an end-of-day entry dated Nov 19. Samsung's page shows $899.75B, up 66% since the start of the year. [Walmart](https://companiesmarketcap.com/walmart/marketcap/), [Samsung](https://companiesmarketcap.com/samsung/marketcap/)
- I could not find a downloadable data file. The page text dropped the up/down signs on the daily % changes, so I can't tell which direction each name moved today.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The count stands at 15, and Walmart is the name most likely to flip it. Anthropic's CMC figure ($1.207T at $91.35) appears to use the basic share count, about 13.2B shares. If CMC switched to the fully diluted count, Anthropic would be about $1.7T.
- The question's background said that in October Berkshire, Lilly, Samsung, Micron and Walmart were all near but presumably below $1T. Since then, Berkshire, Lilly and Walmart have crossed above it, and Anthropic listed. So the count has moved by about 3-4 in roughly a month.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-first-day-trading-nasdaq-record-valuation/), [JoongAng](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/world/anthropic-pulled-off-the-biggest-ipo-ever-what-that-means-by-the-numbers/12982251)
- 2026-11-19: Walmart was scheduled to report Q3 FY27 results that morning. I found no coverage of the actual results or the stock's reaction. [Finviz](https://finviz.com/news/421667/walmart-to-host-third-quarter-earnings-conference-call-november-19-2026)
- 2026-11-19/20: An overnight summary says the S&P 500 fell for a sixth straight session. Chicago Fed President Goolsbee would not rule out a larger-than-usual rate hike. SpaceX plans at least $32B of debt financing. [Longbridge](https://longbridge.com/en/news/306185557)
- 2026-11-18: The Dow fell 561 points to 50,198 and the Nasdaq rose 0.4% after Nvidia's earnings beat. [Zaikei](https://www.zaikei.co.jp/article/20261119/878307.html), [IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.com/us-stocks-dow-falls-nvidia-earnings-fed-rate-hikes-3809938)
- 2026-11-18: UBS set a base-case S&P 500 target of 8,200 for Dec 2027, with 5,500 in an "AI bust" scenario. [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/s-and-p-500-could-hit-8-200-by-end-of-2027-says-ubs-warns-of-5-500-in-ai-bust-scenario/cNbgEIMR9LM)
- 2026-11-17: Another selloff in AI stocks. [WSMV](https://www.wsmv.com/2026/11/17/another-wipeout-hits-wall-street-nvidia-other-jittery-ai-stocks-swing-lower/)
- 2026-11-05: AI stocks lost about $1.8T in one session, the Nasdaq's largest one-day dollar drop ever. [Medium](https://medium.com/@jmh_strong/where-the-value-lies-in-todays-ai-investments-7338368e1d6d)
- 2026-10-29: Samsung fell 4.1% to 232,000 won after disappointing Q3 results. Its record close was 349,000 won on June 1. [JoongAng](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/kospi-falls-124-as-samsung-disappoints-on-shareholder-returns/12945895), [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/amp/economy/others/20260601/samsung-electronics-surge-sends-kospi-above-8800-intraday-for-1st-time)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-02-03: Walmart first closed above $1T, at $127.71. It is now about $129.5, so it has hovered around the threshold all year. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/2/3/walmart-hits-trillion-dollar-market-cap-for-the-first-time)
- Samsung crossed $1T on 2026-02-26 by CMC's measure (preferred shares included), on 2026-05-06 by the Reuters measure, and again around 2026-10-18. It is now about $0.9T. [Asiae](https://cm.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026022617192575007), [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/20260506156/samsungs-market-value-hits-1-trillion), [AIM](https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/samsung-becomes-the-first-south-korean-firm-to-cross-1-tn-market-cap)
- One source put the club at 15 members at the end of October 2026; I could not verify that. [search summary](https://countly.net/most-valuable-companies-2026-trillion-dollar-club)
- On variation: big-cap stocks typically move about ±5-10% over four weeks, and memory chip names (Samsung, Micron) have moved ±20% or more. Over a month that is enough to flip a name within about 5% of the line (Walmart) and sometimes one within 10-15% (Samsung).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the number of trillion-dollar companies. None of the markets supplied matches this question. The closest is a Kalshi market on Elon Musk's net worth on Dec 31 (66% for above $800B), which bears only indirectly on SpaceX's valuation.
- A Motley Fool piece (2026-11-19) pitches an unnamed stock as a future $1T company. [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/19/1-unstoppable-stock-to-buy-before-it-joins-hot-tickers-in-the-1-3-trillion-club/)

## 6. Upcoming events before Dec 18
- Fed meeting around Dec 15-16. Fed-funds markets already price about 98% chance of no cuts in 2026, and officials are openly discussing hikes.
- Micron reports fiscal Q1 earnings around mid-December (date not confirmed), which matters for Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix. Broadcom's earnings are expected around early-to-mid December. Oracle's earnings may also land in December.
- Anthropic's IPO volatility, and whether CMC changes the share count it uses for Anthropic.
- The Korean won and the Saudi riyal peg feed into USD market caps for Samsung and Aramco.
- Dec 18 is a quarterly options-expiration day, which can add to volatility.
- Further AI-sector selloffs like those on Nov 5 and Nov 17 would mostly threaten Walmart's spot through general market weakness. Names with 17%+ of room would need a deep correction to fall out.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-20 (intraday, during US trading): the [CompaniesMarketCap](https://companiesmarketcap.com/) homepage lists **15 companies above $1T**: Apple $5.076T, Microsoft $3.729T, NVIDIA $3.422T, Alphabet $3.421T, Amazon $2.793T, SpaceX $1.802T, TSMC $1.769T, Saudi Aramco $1.707T, Broadcom $1.580T, Meta $1.498T, Tesla $1.470T, Berkshire $1.220T, Eli Lilly $1.214T, Anthropic $1.208T (at $91.39) and Walmart $1.028T (at $129.59, +2.82% today).
- The next companies down are Samsung $899.75B, JPMorgan $849.6B, AMD $774.3B, Visa $759.9B and Micron $738.2B. [CMC](https://companiesmarketcap.com/)
- To join, Samsung needs about +11%, JPM about +18%, AMD about +29% and Micron about +35%. To drop out, Walmart would need to fall about 2.7%, Anthropic about 17% (below roughly $75.6, which is under its $83 IPO price), and Lilly or Berkshire about 18%.
- CMC values Anthropic on shares outstanding (about $1.2T), not fully diluted (about $1.75T). This makes Anthropic's count fragile.
- 2026-11-19: CMC shows NVIDIA's end-of-day cap at $3.524T, down 26.1% year to date. Samsung is up 66% year to date. [CMC NVDA](https://companiesmarketcap.com/nvidia/marketcap/), [CMC Samsung](https://companiesmarketcap.com/samsung/marketcap/)
- I could not find a downloadable CSV or JSON behind the CMC pages. The figures above come from the page text.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled yet. The count is 15 right now, and two members are near the edge: Walmart has about a 3% cushion, and Anthropic is a newly listed, volatile stock.
- Samsung is the most likely new entrant (about 10% away).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

## 4. Base rates
- At the end of 2025 there were roughly 11 members: the big tech names plus Tesla, Aramco, Berkshire and Lilly. This is from memory, not a source.
- In 2026 the count grew mainly through IPOs (SpaceX, Anthropic) and Walmart crossing $1T. It was about 14 in mid-November and is 15 now.
- Over a 4-week window, single large-cap stocks typically move ±5-10%. When the VIX is above 30, ±10-15% is plausible. That is enough to push Walmart or Anthropic out, or Samsung in. JPM, AMD and Micron would need unusually large rallies.
- In a broad 5-10% drawdown, Walmart drops out first, then Anthropic. Lilly and Berkshire would need about an 18% fall.

## 5. Other forecasts

## 6. Upcoming events before Dec 18

- Dec 18 is a quarterly options expiration ("triple witching") day, which can bring extra volatility.
- Walmart may face pressure from rate moves and holiday sales data.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 4 weeks of trading (Nov 20 to the Dec 18 close). The question resolves around Dec 19 00:00 UTC.

(b) Status quo: 15 companies are above $1T on CompaniesMarketCap as of Nov 20, 2026, so the status quo answer is "15".

(c) Base rates: Over a one-month window the trillion-dollar count usually changes by 0 or ±1. It changes by 2 or more only during sharp market moves or big IPOs. Names within about 3% of the line flip roughly 35-45% of the time over a month. Names 10-15% away flip roughly 10-20% of the time, more for volatile memory-chip stocks.

(d) Strongest evidence:
- **Walmart (Nov 20):** CMC shows the count at 15, with Walmart at $1.027T, only about 2.6% of cushion. The market is weak: the S&P 500 has fallen six straight sessions and the Fed is talking about rate hikes. Walmart's Nov 19 earnings reaction is unknown.
- **Samsung (Nov 20):** $899.75B, needing about +11%. It is volatile, and Micron's mid-December earnings are a catalyst.
- **Anthropic (listed Nov 19):** $1.207T on basic shares, about 17% of room. New IPOs are highly volatile, but if CMC switched to the fully diluted share count its value would rise, not fall.
- **Other names near the line:**
  - Lilly and Berkshire each have about 17-18% of room.
  - JPMorgan needs about +18%, AMD about +29% and Micron about +36%.

(e) Unexpected scenario: An AI-bust selloff deepens, like the Nov 5 and Nov 17 drops. Walmart slips below the line, Anthropic loses 20% as post-IPO enthusiasm fades, and Lilly drops on a drug-pricing headline. The count falls to 12-13. In the other direction, a memory-chip rally after Micron's earnings could push Samsung over $1T while Walmart holds, giving 16.

Reasoning:
- I estimate Walmart falls out with about 40% probability, Anthropic with about 12%, and Lilly or Berkshire with about 5%.
- I estimate Samsung gets in with about 17% probability, and any of the others (AMD, JPM, Micron) with about 8%.
- Combining these, with some correlation between them, I keep 15 as the modal outcome but give substantial weight to 14.
